code_quality.notes: -4: readAttempts (feedbackgate_stores.go:115-138) and readCount (:212-226) swallow non-NotFound transaction read errors, returning empty window / zero count. The in-code justification ('the transaction commit is what actually reports failure') is not reliable for transient read RPC failures in Firestore native mode: a failed read never reaches the server's validation set, so the commit can SUCCEED and overwrite a populated window with a reset one. Effect: cooldown and budget counters reset exactly during Firestore degradation (fail-open) in a gate whose purpose is flood/cost protection. The cited messaging.go:93 precedent RETURNS such errors (if err != iterator.Done { return err }).

issues.issue: Non-NotFound transaction read errors are swallowed and mapped to an empty window (cooldown) / zero count (budget). Under transient Firestore read failure the transaction commit can still succeed, overwriting the stored window with a reset one — cooldown/budget protection silently resets during infra degradation (fail-open). Violates CLAUDE.md Critical Principle 2 (no silent fallbacks in business logic), contradicts the design doc's 'adapter just returns errors honestly', and deviates from the messaging.go:93 precedent which returns such errors.
issues.suggestion: Change readAttempts to return ([]time.Time, error) and readCount to (int, error); propagate any non-NotFound error out of the transaction fn (RunTransaction aborts/retries; Increment/IncrementDaily return the error; applyCooldown propagates; the M4 wiring already fails CLOSED on gate error with an audit). NotFound remains an empty window/zero count (legitimate first-attempt case). The malformed-field case (attempts not []interface{} / count not numeric) MAY remain a defensive empty/zero — it is deterministic corruption, not transient degradation — but must carry a comment making that decision explicit. Update tests if signatures change; make lint + targeted go test must stay green.
